# Facts That Change {#sec-facts}



Prices, plans, accounts and free allowances change from month to month, so this book keeps
them in one place: a file in its source, `book/facts.yml`, which this appendix prints in full.
The chapters quote it rather than typing a price or a plan, so when a fact changes, one edit
and a rebuild update every page that mentions it, and this list. Each fact carries the date it
was checked against the official page linked beside it. By the time you read this, some will
have changed: follow the link, and trust the page over the book.

## Agents and their accounts {.unnumbered}

**What Claude Code's account must be.** Claude Code needs a Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, Enterprise or Console account. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup).

**What Claude Code costs.** Claude Code, for one, needs a paid plan or pay-per-use billing. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup).

**What Codex's account must be.** Codex needs a ChatGPT sign-in or an API key. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth).

**What Antigravity's account must be.** Antigravity needs a Google account. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://antigravity.google/docs/faq).

**Antigravity's free tier.** A personal Google account can use Antigravity on its free tier, with a quota refreshed weekly. Checked 2026-11-18, sources [1](https://antigravity.google/docs/plans), [2](https://antigravity.google/docs/faq).

**What OpenCode's account must be.** OpenCode needs a provider connected from inside it with /connect: a ChatGPT plan, GitHub Copilot, an API key, a local model or an OpenCode account. Checked 2026-11-20, [source](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/).

**OpenCode's free models.** OpenCode lists models that are free for a limited time once an OpenCode account is connected, and the list changes from week to week. Checked 2026-11-20, sources [1](https://opencode.ai/docs/models/), [2](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/).

**What OpenCode asks before acting.** OpenCode's default agent edits files and runs commands without asking, inside the folder or outside it, unless rules with the effect ask are added to opencode.jsonc. Checked 2026-11-20, sources [1](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/), [2](https://opencode.ai/docs/agents/).

**A spending cap for Claude Code on API billing.** A Claude Console account can cap Claude Code's monthly spending with a workspace spend limit. Checked 2026-11-18, sources [1](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs), [2](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/workspaces).

**A spending cap for Codex on API billing.** An OpenAI API organization or project can set a hard monthly spend limit, after which requests stop. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/spend-limits).

**When Antigravity replaced Gemini CLI.** Antigravity replaced Gemini CLI for unpaid-tier and Google One users on 18 June 2026. Checked 2026-11-12, [source](https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/installation).

**Where Codex looks for AGENTS.md.** Codex reads `AGENTS.md` files before doing any work. Checked 2026-10-30, [source](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md).

**Where Antigravity looks for AGENTS.md.** Antigravity reads `AGENTS.md` or `GEMINI.md` in the project's folders. Checked 2026-10-30, [source](https://antigravity.google/docs/rules).

**Where OpenCode looks for AGENTS.md.** OpenCode reads each `AGENTS.md` from the working folder upwards, and `CLAUDE.md` in a folder without one. Checked 2026-11-20, [source](https://opencode.ai/docs/rules/).

**Where Claude Code looks for AGENTS.md.** Claude Code reads `AGENTS.md` when there is no `CLAUDE.md` in the working folder or above it, from version 2.1.277, and a `CLAUDE.md` containing the line `@AGENTS.md` imports it. Checked 2026-11-12, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory).

**How Claude Code is installed.** Its installer is `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh \| bash`. Checked 2026-10-30, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup).

**How Codex is installed.** Its installer is `curl -fsSL https://chatgpt.com/codex/install.sh \| sh`. Checked 2026-10-30, [source](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/codex/cli).

**How Antigravity is installed.** Its installer is `curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh \| bash`. Checked 2026-10-30, [source](https://antigravity.google/docs/getting-started?tab=cli).

**How OpenCode is installed.** Its installer is `curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install \| bash`. Checked 2026-11-20, [source](https://opencode.ai/docs/).

## GitHub's free allowances {.unnumbered}

**GitHub Codespaces on a free personal account.** A free personal GitHub account includes 120 hours of Codespaces compute a month, counted twice over on the default two-core machine, so about 60 hours of use, and 15 GB of storage. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/managing-billing-for-your-products/managing-billing-for-github-codespaces/about-billing-for-github-codespaces).

**GitHub Pages for private repositories.** A free GitHub account publishes Pages from public repositories only; private repositories need a paid plan, and a site only your organisation can see needs GitHub Enterprise Cloud. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/learning-about-github/githubs-plans).

**GitHub Actions on a free account.** GitHub Actions' standard runners are free in public repositories, and a free account's private repositories get 12 US dollars of compute a month. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions).

**Protected branches on a free account.** On a free GitHub account, protected branches and rulesets work in public repositories only; private repositories need GitHub Pro, Team or Enterprise. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches).

## Free web chats {.unnumbered}

**Web chats with a free plan.** Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini each have a free plan. Checked 2026-11-12, sources [1](https://claude.com/pricing), [2](https://chatgpt.com/pricing), [3](https://gemini.google/subscriptions/).

## Models and their prices {.unnumbered}

**Models enough for this book's prompts.** Claude's Sonnet on medium effort, or Haiku for small edits, or OpenAI's Sol on low. Checked 2026-11-12, sources [1](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview), [2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models).

**Where the vendors suggest starting for hard work.** Anthropic suggests starting with Opus 5.5 for most workloads, and OpenAI with GPT-6 Astra for complex reasoning and coding. Checked 2026-11-12, sources [1](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview), [2](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models).

## What the vendors do with your data {.unnumbered}

**Claude's consumer plans.** On Anthropic's Free, Pro, Max and Ultra plans, Claude Code included, conversations are used to train new models when the user's privacy setting allows it, and are kept for five years when it does, thirty days when it does not. Checked 2026-11-24, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage).

**Claude's commercial plans and the API.** Under Anthropic's commercial terms (Team, Enterprise, the API), code and prompts are not used for training unless the customer opts in, and are kept thirty days by default; zero data retention is available to qualified Enterprise accounts. Checked 2026-11-24, sources [1](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage), [2](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/zero-data-retention).

**What Claude Code keeps on your computer.** Claude Code keeps session transcripts in plain text under ~/.claude/projects/ for thirty days by default. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/data-usage).

**OpenAI's API.** Data sent to OpenAI's API is not used for training unless you opt in; abuse-monitoring logs are kept up to thirty days, and zero data retention needs OpenAI's approval. Checked 2026-11-24, [source](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data).

**ChatGPT's business plans.** ChatGPT Business, Enterprise and Edu workspace data is not used to train OpenAI's models by default. Checked 2026-11-24, sources [1](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-cloud-security), [2](https://openai.com/enterprise-privacy/).

**Which policy Codex follows.** How you sign in to Codex, with a ChatGPT plan or an API key, decides which data policy applies. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth).

**Antigravity's terms.** Antigravity's terms say Google uses interactions to improve its products, its employees and contractors may review them, and users can opt out in settings; they ask users not to submit confidential information. Checked 2026-11-24, [source](https://antigravity.google/terms).

**What OpenCode's free models keep.** With a provider you connect, that provider's terms apply; of OpenCode's free models, some keep prompts and may use them to improve the model, and NVIDIA's trial endpoints ask users not to submit personal or confidential data. Checked 2026-11-20, [source](https://opencode.ai/docs/zen/).

## The tools' licences {.unnumbered}

**Quarto's licence.** Quarto is published under the MIT License. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://quarto.org/license.html).

**Pandoc's licence.** Pandoc is published under the GNU GPL. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://github.com/jgm/pandoc/blob/main/COPYRIGHT).

**Typst's licence.** Typst is published under the Apache License 2.0. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://github.com/typst/typst/blob/main/LICENSE).

**Codex CLI's licence.** OpenAI's Codex CLI is published under the Apache License 2.0. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://github.com/openai/codex).

**Gemini CLI's licence.** Google's Gemini CLI was published under the Apache License 2.0. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli).

**Claude Code's licence.** Anthropic's Claude Code is not open source. Checked 2026-11-18, [source](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code).

**OpenCode's licence.** OpenCode is published under the MIT License. Checked 2026-11-20, [source](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode).



## Model prices {.unnumbered}

| Model | Input / output, \$ per million tokens |
|---|---|
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | 0.10 / 0.50 |
| Claude Sonnet 5.5 | 2 / 10 |
| Claude Opus 5.5 | 4 / 20 |
| Claude Fable 5.2 | 8 / 40 |
| GPT-6 Luna | 0.10 / 0.50 |
| GPT-6.1 Terra | 1 / 5 |
| GPT-6.1 Sol | 2 / 10 |
| GPT-6 Astra | 10 / 50 |

: List prices of eight models, in dollars per million tokens of input and output, checked 2026-11-12. {#tbl-prices}

Haiku's price is for prompts up to 100,000 tokens; longer ones cost five times as much. Subscriptions count usage differently from API prices, and which models you can choose depends on your plan and the agent's version.

What each vendor says its model is for:

::: cards
Claude Haiku 5.5
:   "high-volume, latency-sensitive tasks such as classification, extraction, and routing"

Claude Sonnet 5.5
:   "the best combination of speed and intelligence"

Claude Opus 5.5
:   "long-running agentic coding and knowledge work"

Claude Fable 5.2
:   "demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work"

GPT-6 Luna
:   "focused, high-volume tasks"

GPT-6.1 Terra
:   "visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clear, natural writing"

GPT-6.1 Sol
:   "near-Astra performance for complex work at a lower cost"

GPT-6 Astra
:   "the most demanding work"

:::

Sources: Anthropic's [pricing](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) and [models](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview) pages and OpenAI's [models](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) pages.


These are *API* prices: what a program pays per token when it calls the model directly
(@sec-choose). Read them as a snapshot of the spread between small and large models, not as
numbers to plan with.

@sec-hosting explains the two ways these hosts work: you render and upload, or they build
from your repository.
